questions.q: What is a connection manager, precisely?
options: A design-time, logical description of a connection — the physical connection is created at run time from its properties
The physical, live connection itself, open for the life of the package
A type of task that only appears in the Data Flow tab
A file format for storing SQL Server backups
questions.explain: A connection manager is a logical representation set at design time (e.g. its ConnectionString property); Integration Services uses those properties to create the real connection when the package runs.

questions.q: Where does the Connection Managers area appear in SSIS Designer?
options: Docked along the bottom of the Control Flow, Data Flow, and Event Handlers tabs
Only inside the SSIS Toolbox
In a separate standalone application outside Visual Studio
Only on the Package Explorer tab
questions.explain: The Connection Managers area is available whenever the Control Flow, Data Flow, or Event Handlers tab is active.

questions.q: What's different about a connection manager created at the project level versus the package level?
options: A project-level one is shared by every package in the project and shows up with a (project) prefix in each package's Connection Managers area
A project-level connection manager can only be used by one package, chosen at creation time
There is no difference — SSIS doesn't support project-level connection managers
Project-level connection managers can't be renamed or edited after creation
questions.explain: Project-level connection managers, created in Solution Explorer, are shared across every package in the project and appear with a (project) prefix that can't be overwritten from inside a package.

questions.q: How do you open the Add SSIS Connection Manager dialog box to see every built-in connection type?
options: Right-click in the Connection Managers area and select New Connection
Open the Properties window and click Connections
Select File > New > Connection Manager from the main menu
It opens automatically the first time you create a project
questions.explain: Right-clicking in the Connection Managers area and choosing New Connection opens the Add SSIS Connection Manager dialog box, listing every built-in type.

questions.q: Can a single package use more than one instance of the same connection manager type?
options: Yes — for example, two separate OLE DB connection managers pointed at two different databases
No — each connection manager type can only be used once per package
Only if the two instances are on the same server
Only for Flat File connection managers, never OLE DB
questions.explain: A package can use multiple instances of a connection manager type, each with its own independently configured properties.
